mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an active monetary easing cycle, which reduces discount rates applied to future equity cash flows and increases the present value of S&P 500 earnings, leading to positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% within a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which triggers risk-off sentiment and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0% over 3 months, or the signal fails to outperform baseline in walk-forward IC tests.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential investment (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based contraction in private demand, which signals weakening economic activity and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03), or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (2017=100) combined with a concurrent rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a supply-side shock coupled with labor market stress, which increases recession risk and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO < 100 and UNRATE > 3.5% occur simultaneously (t-test p > 0.05), or the interaction signal has Rank IC < 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with rising housing starts (HOUST), signals strong underlying demand momentum, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal fails to predict positive 5-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03), or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05) in walk-forward testing.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 2.0% within a 3-month window signals a tightening monetary policy regime, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during FEDFUNDS > 2.0% periods (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal has Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) below 50,000 in a month signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS < 50.0 (in thousands), or the signal fails to achieve Rank IC > 0.03 in walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) below its 4-quarter moving average, combined with a decline in residential investment (HOUST), indicates a deepening demand slump, which triggers equity market sell-offs and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03), or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample testing.
